manifest.honesty_label: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Sorafenib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Axitinib, Pazopanib, Sunitinib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Vasculature: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (77%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Blood / immune: moderate predicted involvement (51%), driven mainly by the MAPK feedback, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.625), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Angiogenesis / endothelial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.563), consistent with an anti-angiogenic action.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Vismodegib) and phenotype anchor (Axitinib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (84%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Sorafenib — VEGFR / multi-TKI
step6_report.mechanism_text: Sorafenib (VEGFR / multi-TKI) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as LDHA, CA9, EGLN3; most repressed include KDR, FLT1, DUSP6.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Axitinib (phenotype similarity 0.839); nearest-atlas distance 0.161 places Sorafenib in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Sorafenib nearest Vismodegib (Hedgehog / Notch); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Axitinib (VEGFR / multi-TKI). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Sunitinib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Axitinib, Pazopanib, Sorafenib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Vasculature: strong predicted involvement (98%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (93%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, MAPK feedback program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.579), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The Angiogenesis / endothelial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.578), consistent with an anti-angiogenic action.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Lidocaine) and phenotype anchor (Axitinib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (82%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Sunitinib — VEGFR / multi-TKI
step6_report.mechanism_text: Sunitinib (VEGFR / multi-TKI) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as OAS1, STAT1, NDRG1; most repressed include ANGPT2, TEK, NRP1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Axitinib (phenotype similarity 0.82); nearest-atlas distance 0.18 places Sunitinib in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Sunitinib nearest Lidocaine (Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Axitinib (VEGFR / multi-TKI). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Axitinib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Pazopanib, Sorafenib, Sunitinib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Vasculature: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (93%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Blood / immune: moderate predicted involvement (62%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, MAPK feedback program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.
The Angiogenesis / endothelial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.558), consistent with an anti-angiogenic action.
The Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.49), reshaping lipid metabolism.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Vismodegib) and phenotype anchor (Pazopanib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (88%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Axitinib — VEGFR / multi-TKI
step6_report.mechanism_text: Axitinib (VEGFR / multi-TKI) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as PDK1, EGLN3, NDRG1; most repressed include FLT1, CDH5, KDR.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Pazopanib (phenotype similarity 0.878); nearest-atlas distance 0.122 places Axitinib in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Axitinib nearest Vismodegib (Hedgehog / Notch); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Pazopanib (VEGFR / multi-TKI). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Pazopanib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Axitinib, Sorafenib, Sunitinib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Vasculature: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (91%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Glucocorticoid / NR response program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (74%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.
The Angiogenesis / endothelial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.596), consistent with an anti-angiogenic action.
The Translation / ribosome program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.548), throttling protein-synthesis capacity.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Celecoxib) and phenotype anchor (Axitinib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (88%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Pazopanib — VEGFR / multi-TKI
step6_report.mechanism_text: Pazopanib (VEGFR / multi-TKI) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as ADM, LDHA, PDK1; most repressed include CDH5, FLT1, DDIT4.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Axitinib (phenotype similarity 0.878); nearest-atlas distance 0.122 places Pazopanib in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Pazopanib nearest Celecoxib (NSAID); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Axitinib (VEGFR / multi-TKI). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Panobinostat directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Vorinostat, Romidepsin, Paclitaxel). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (86%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (49%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.821), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.683), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Curcumin) and phenotype anchor (Vorinostat) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (90%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Panobinostat — HDAC inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Panobinostat (HDAC inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAX, TIGAR, BBC3; most repressed include AURKA, FOXM1, CDK1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Vorinostat (phenotype similarity 0.904); nearest-atlas distance 0.096 places Panobinostat in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Panobinostat nearest Curcumin (Natural product); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Vorinostat (HDAC inhibitor). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Vorinostat directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Romidepsin, Panobinostat, Entinostat). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (95%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (60%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.766), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.748), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Lidocaine) and phenotype anchor (Romidepsin) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (95%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Vorinostat — HDAC inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Vorinostat (HDAC inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BBC3, BAX, RRM2B; most repressed include PCNA, BUB1, CCNB2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Romidepsin (phenotype similarity 0.951); nearest-atlas distance 0.049 places Vorinostat in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Vorinostat nearest Lidocaine (Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Romidepsin (HDAC inhibitor). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Entinostat directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Romidepsin, Vorinostat, Panobinostat). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (80%), driven mainly by the Interferon / inflammatory, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.79), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.722), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Vorinostat) and phenotype anchor (Romidepsin) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (89%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Entinostat — HDAC inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Entinostat (HDAC inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAX, ZMAT3, TIGAR; most repressed include CCNB1, CCNB2, BUB1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Romidepsin (phenotype similarity 0.887); nearest-atlas distance 0.113 places Entinostat in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Entinostat nearest Vorinostat (HDAC inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Romidepsin (HDAC inhibitor). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Romidepsin directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Vorinostat, Panobinostat, Entinostat). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (81%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (52%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.824), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.704), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Cyclosporin A) and phenotype anchor (Vorinostat) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (95%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Romidepsin — HDAC inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Romidepsin (HDAC inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BBC3, BAX, TIGAR; most repressed include PCNA, PLK1, TYMS.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Vorinostat (phenotype similarity 0.951); nearest-atlas distance 0.049 places Romidepsin in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Romidepsin nearest Cyclosporin A (Immunosuppressant); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Vorinostat (HDAC inhibitor). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Rapamycin directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Everolimus, Idelalisib, Omipalisib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP, PI3K–AKT–mTOR program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (60%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Translation / ribosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Brain / CNS: moderate predicted involvement (56%), driven mainly by the PI3K–AKT–mTOR, Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The PI3K–AKT–mTOR program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.809), tuning the PI3K–AKT–mTOR growth axis.
The Translation / ribosome program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.59), throttling protein-synthesis capacity.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Everolimus) and phenotype anchor (Everolimus) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (88%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Rapamycin — PI3K / mTOR
step6_report.mechanism_text: Rapamycin (PI3K / mTOR) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as ATG12, CTSD, WIPI1; most repressed include EIF4EBP1, SLC2A1, INSIG1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Everolimus (phenotype similarity 0.875); nearest-atlas distance 0.125 places Rapamycin in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Rapamycin nearest Everolimus (PI3K / mTOR); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Everolimus (PI3K / mTOR). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Everolimus directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Idelalisib, Omipalisib, Rapamycin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the PI3K–AKT–mTOR, Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (73%), driven mainly by the Autophagy / lysosome, PI3K–AKT–mTOR program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (66%), driven mainly by the Translation / ribosome, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The PI3K–AKT–mTOR program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.746), tuning the PI3K–AKT–mTOR growth axis.
The Autophagy / lysosome program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.515), inducing autophagy/lysosomal turnover.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Rapamycin) and phenotype anchor (Idelalisib) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (89%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Everolimus — PI3K / mTOR
step6_report.mechanism_text: Everolimus (PI3K / mTOR) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as WIPI1, LAMP1, MAP1LC3B; most repressed include EIF4EBP1, TXNIP, SLC2A1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Idelalisib (phenotype similarity 0.891); nearest-atlas distance 0.109 places Everolimus in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Everolimus nearest Rapamycin (PI3K / mTOR); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Idelalisib (PI3K / mTOR). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Idelalisib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Everolimus, Rapamycin, Omipalisib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the PI3K–AKT–mTOR, Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (69%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Translation / ribosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (66%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Translation / ribosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The PI3K–AKT–mTOR program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.797), tuning the PI3K–AKT–mTOR growth axis.
The Translation / ribosome program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.618), throttling protein-synthesis capacity.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Roscovitine) and phenotype anchor (Everolimus) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (89%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Idelalisib — PI3K / mTOR
step6_report.mechanism_text: Idelalisib (PI3K / mTOR) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as LAMP1, SQSTM1, TFEB; most repressed include EIF4EBP1, SESN2, INSR.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Everolimus (phenotype similarity 0.891); nearest-atlas distance 0.109 places Idelalisib in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Idelalisib nearest Roscovitine (CDK inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Everolimus (PI3K / mTOR). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Omipalisib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Everolimus, Rapamycin, Idelalisib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the PI3K–AKT–mTOR, Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (71%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Translation / ribosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (64%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Translation / ribosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.826), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
The PI3K–AKT–mTOR program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.647), tuning the PI3K–AKT–mTOR growth axis.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Pazopanib) and phenotype anchor (Everolimus) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (89%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound

step6_report.headline: Omipalisib — PI3K / mTOR
step6_report.mechanism_text: Omipalisib (PI3K / mTOR) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as GABARAPL1, ATG12, CTSB; most repressed include EIF4EBP1, PCK2, IRS2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Everolimus (phenotype similarity 0.891); nearest-atlas distance 0.109 places Omipalisib in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Omipalisib nearest Pazopanib (VEGFR / multi-TKI); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Everolimus (PI3K / mTOR). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Enalapril directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Ramipril, Propranolol, Valsartan). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (85%), driven mainly by the Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (81%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.587), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.371), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Ramipril) and phenotype anchor (Ramipril) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (61%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Enalapril — RAAS inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Enalapril (RAAS inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as CTSD, SLC2A1, GABARAPL1; most repressed include CPT1A, ELOVL6, ACOX1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Ramipril (phenotype similarity 0.614); nearest-atlas distance 0.386 places Enalapril in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Enalapril nearest Ramipril (RAAS inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Ramipril (RAAS inhibitor). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Ramipril directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Losartan, Enalapril, Valsartan). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Vasculature: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (97%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (76%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.523), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.348), reshaping lipid metabolism.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Enalapril) and phenotype anchor (Losartan) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (74%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Ramipril — RAAS inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Ramipril (RAAS inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BNIP3, NDRG1, FOXO3; most repressed include IL1B, TNFAIP3, CXCL8.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Losartan (phenotype similarity 0.74); nearest-atlas distance 0.26 places Ramipril in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Ramipril nearest Enalapril (RAAS inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Losartan (RAAS inhibitor). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Losartan directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Ramipril, Valsartan, Celecoxib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Glucocorticoid / NR response program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Vasculature: strong predicted involvement (95%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (79%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.561), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.415), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Valsartan) and phenotype anchor (Ramipril) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (74%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Losartan — RAAS inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Losartan (RAAS inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as PDK1, BNIP3, GREB1; most repressed include CXCL1, BIRC3, NFKBIA.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Ramipril (phenotype similarity 0.74); nearest-atlas distance 0.26 places Losartan in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Losartan nearest Valsartan (RAAS inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Ramipril (RAAS inhibitor). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Valsartan directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Losartan, Ticagrelor, Metformin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Vasculature: strong predicted involvement (85%), driven mainly by the Hypoxia, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (73%), driven mainly by the Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The OXPHOS / mitochondrial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.685), shifting mitochondrial / OXPHOS activity.
The Angiogenesis / endothelial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.43), consistent with an anti-angiogenic action.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Losartan) and phenotype anchor (Losartan) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (63%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Valsartan — RAAS inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Valsartan (RAAS inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BNIP3, PGK1, CA9; most repressed include CCL2, CXCL1, ACACA.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Losartan (phenotype similarity 0.634); nearest-atlas distance 0.366 places Valsartan in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Valsartan nearest Losartan (RAAS inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Losartan (RAAS inhibitor). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Simvastatin directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Lovastatin, Atorvastatin, Pravastatin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP, Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (47%), driven mainly by the Apoptosis, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Blood / immune: moderate predicted involvement (43%), driven mainly by the Apoptosis, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.
The Proteostasis / heat-shock program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.973), triggering a proteostasis / heat-shock response.
The Cholesterol / SREBP program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.799), engaging the cholesterol-biosynthesis feedback axis.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Lovastatin) and phenotype anchor (Lovastatin) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (81%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Simvastatin — Statin
step6_report.mechanism_text: Simvastatin (Statin) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as HMGCR, FDFT1, FDPS; most repressed include TXNIP, TSC22D3, SGK1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Lovastatin (phenotype similarity 0.813); nearest-atlas distance 0.187 places Simvastatin in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Simvastatin nearest Lovastatin (Statin); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Lovastatin (Statin). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Atorvastatin directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Pravastatin, Lovastatin, Simvastatin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP, Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (43%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Vasculature: moderate predicted involvement (43%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.
The Cholesterol / SREBP program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.708), engaging the cholesterol-biosynthesis feedback axis.
The Apoptosis program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.522), priming cells toward programmed death.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Pravastatin) and phenotype anchor (Pravastatin) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (86%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Atorvastatin — Statin
step6_report.mechanism_text: Atorvastatin (Statin) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as FDFT1, LDLR, HMGCR; most repressed include TNFAIP3, MYB, BIRC3.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Pravastatin (phenotype similarity 0.861); nearest-atlas distance 0.139 places Atorvastatin in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Atorvastatin nearest Pravastatin (Statin); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Pravastatin (Statin). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Pravastatin directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Atorvastatin, Lovastatin, Simvastatin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP, Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (58%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Vasculature: moderate predicted involvement (40%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP, Angiogenesis / endothelial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.
The Cholesterol / SREBP program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.729), engaging the cholesterol-biosynthesis feedback axis.
The Autophagy / lysosome program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.397), inducing autophagy/lysosomal turnover.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Lovastatin) and phenotype anchor (Atorvastatin) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (86%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Pravastatin — Statin
step6_report.mechanism_text: Pravastatin (Statin) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as FDPS, SQLE, HMGCS1; most repressed include RPLP0, RPL11, NDRG1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Atorvastatin (phenotype similarity 0.861); nearest-atlas distance 0.139 places Pravastatin in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Pravastatin nearest Lovastatin (Statin); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Atorvastatin (Statin). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Lovastatin directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Atorvastatin, Simvastatin, Pravastatin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP, Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (34%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Vasculature: mild predicted involvement (29%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.
The Cholesterol / SREBP program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.687), engaging the cholesterol-biosynthesis feedback axis.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.391), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Simvastatin) and phenotype anchor (Atorvastatin) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (85%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Lovastatin — Statin
step6_report.mechanism_text: Lovastatin (Statin) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as SQLE, FDPS, SREBF2; most repressed include DDIT4, TXNIP, BNIP3.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Atorvastatin (phenotype similarity 0.846); nearest-atlas distance 0.154 places Lovastatin in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Lovastatin nearest Simvastatin (Statin); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Atorvastatin (Statin). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Fluoxetine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Paroxetine, Clozapine, Nifedipine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Autophagy / lysosome, OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (91%), driven mainly by the Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Skeletal muscle: strong predicted involvement (85%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as muscle/somite integrity or metabolic load.
The Proteostasis / heat-shock program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.363), triggering a proteostasis / heat-shock response.
The Cholesterol / SREBP program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.361), engaging the cholesterol-biosynthesis feedback axis.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (DAPT) and phenotype anchor (Paroxetine) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (69%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Fluoxetine — SSRI
step6_report.mechanism_text: Fluoxetine (SSRI) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as MAP1LC3B, TCF7, CTSD; most repressed include MRPL13, COX5A, COX6C.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Paroxetine (phenotype similarity 0.689); nearest-atlas distance 0.311 places Fluoxetine in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Fluoxetine nearest DAPT (Hedgehog / Notch); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Paroxetine (SSRI). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

narrative: We don't measure Sertraline directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Rapamycin, Everolimus, Fluoxetine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (72%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

The Translation / ribosome program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.577), throttling protein-synthesis capacity.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Paroxetine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Fluoxetine, Nifedipine, Lidocaine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Skeletal muscle: strong predicted involvement (88%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as muscle/somite integrity or metabolic load.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (70%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.
The Cholesterol / SREBP program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.392), engaging the cholesterol-biosynthesis feedback axis.
The Proteostasis / heat-shock program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.363), triggering a proteostasis / heat-shock response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Niraparib) and phenotype anchor (Fluoxetine) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (69%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Paroxetine — SSRI
step6_report.mechanism_text: Paroxetine (SSRI) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as ATG12, GLB1, CTSB; most repressed include CYC1, ATP5F1A, NDUFA4.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Fluoxetine (phenotype similarity 0.689); nearest-atlas distance 0.311 places Paroxetine in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Paroxetine nearest Niraparib (PARP inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Fluoxetine (SSRI). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Aspirin directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Ibuprofen, Pimecrolimus, Cyclosporin A). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (58%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (49%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.75), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.508), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Vorinostat) and phenotype anchor (Ibuprofen) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (79%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Aspirin — NSAID
step6_report.mechanism_text: Aspirin (NSAID) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAX, BBC3, BCL2; most repressed include TNF, CCL2, CXCL1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Ibuprofen (phenotype similarity 0.787); nearest-atlas distance 0.213 places Aspirin in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Aspirin nearest Vorinostat (HDAC inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Ibuprofen (NSAID). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.
