narrative: We don't measure Ibuprofen directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Aspirin, Leflunomide, Pimecrolimus). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (66%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (62%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.73), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.547), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Atenolol) and phenotype anchor (Aspirin) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (79%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Ibuprofen — NSAID
step6_report.mechanism_text: Ibuprofen (NSAID) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAK1, BAX, BCL2L11; most repressed include SOD2, TNFAIP3, NFKB1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Aspirin (phenotype similarity 0.787); nearest-atlas distance 0.213 places Ibuprofen in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Ibuprofen nearest Atenolol (β-adrenergic); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Aspirin (NSAID). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Celecoxib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Aspirin, Ibuprofen, Leflunomide). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (83%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (57%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.821), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.558), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Avagacestat) and phenotype anchor (Aspirin) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (73%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Celecoxib — NSAID
step6_report.mechanism_text: Celecoxib (NSAID) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as SLC2A1, PDK1, CASP3; most repressed include TNFAIP3, CXCL8, CCL2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Aspirin (phenotype similarity 0.728); nearest-atlas distance 0.272 places Celecoxib in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Celecoxib nearest Avagacestat (Hedgehog / Notch); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Aspirin (NSAID). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Dexamethasone directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Prednisone, Hydrocortisone, Budesonide). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Glucocorticoid / NR response program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (64%), driven mainly by the Glucocorticoid / NR response, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (53%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.695), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.586), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Prednisone) and phenotype anchor (Prednisone) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (87%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Dexamethasone — Glucocorticoid
step6_report.mechanism_text: Dexamethasone (Glucocorticoid) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as DDIT4, ZBTB16, PER1; most repressed include NFKB1, IL1B, TNF.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Prednisone (phenotype similarity 0.867); nearest-atlas distance 0.133 places Dexamethasone in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Dexamethasone nearest Prednisone (Glucocorticoid); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Prednisone (Glucocorticoid). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Prednisone directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Dexamethasone, Hydrocortisone, Budesonide). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Glucocorticoid / NR response, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (62%), driven mainly by the Glucocorticoid / NR response, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (40%), driven mainly by the Apoptosis, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.717), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Glucocorticoid / NR response program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.558), a steroid-receptor / anti-inflammatory signature.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Hydrocortisone) and phenotype anchor (Dexamethasone) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (87%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Prednisone — Glucocorticoid
step6_report.mechanism_text: Prednisone (Glucocorticoid) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as FKBP5, PER1, TSC22D3; most repressed include OAS1, IRF7, IER3.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Dexamethasone (phenotype similarity 0.867); nearest-atlas distance 0.133 places Prednisone in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Prednisone nearest Hydrocortisone (Glucocorticoid); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Dexamethasone (Glucocorticoid). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Hydrocortisone directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Dexamethasone, Prednisone, Leflunomide). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Glucocorticoid / NR response program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (70%), driven mainly by the Glucocorticoid / NR response, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (49%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.776), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.614), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Prednisone) and phenotype anchor (Dexamethasone) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (85%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Hydrocortisone — Glucocorticoid
step6_report.mechanism_text: Hydrocortisone (Glucocorticoid) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as DDIT4, FKBP5, PER1; most repressed include CXCL8, RELB, OAS2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Dexamethasone (phenotype similarity 0.852); nearest-atlas distance 0.148 places Hydrocortisone in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Hydrocortisone nearest Prednisone (Glucocorticoid); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Dexamethasone (Glucocorticoid). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Dapagliflozin directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Orlistat, Metformin, Pioglitazone). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (96%), driven mainly by the Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism, OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Skeletal muscle: strong predicted involvement (77%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Proteostasis / heat-shock program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as muscle/somite integrity or metabolic load.
The Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.571), reshaping lipid metabolism.
The OXPHOS / mitochondrial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.431), shifting mitochondrial / OXPHOS activity.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Sertraline) and phenotype anchor (Orlistat) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (76%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step6_report.headline: Dapagliflozin — Antidiabetic
step6_report.mechanism_text: Dapagliflozin (Antidiabetic) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as ATF3, PDK1, BAG3; most repressed include FASN, CPT1A, DGAT1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Orlistat (phenotype similarity 0.756); nearest-atlas distance 0.244 places Dapagliflozin in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Dapagliflozin nearest Sertraline (SSRI); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Orlistat (Antidiabetic). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Pioglitazone directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Orlistat, Glibenclamide, Metformin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism, Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (77%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Vasculature: moderate predicted involvement (57%), driven mainly by the Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.
The Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.537), reshaping lipid metabolism.
The OXPHOS / mitochondrial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.443), shifting mitochondrial / OXPHOS activity.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Dofetilide) and phenotype anchor (Orlistat) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (79%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Glibenclamide directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Orlistat, Metformin, Pioglitazone). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism, Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (84%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Blood / immune: moderate predicted involvement (56%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.
The Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.541), reshaping lipid metabolism.
The OXPHOS / mitochondrial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.423), shifting mitochondrial / OXPHOS activity.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Ixazomib) and phenotype anchor (Orlistat) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (78%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Glibenclamide — Antidiabetic
step6_report.mechanism_text: Glibenclamide (Antidiabetic) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as HMOX1, LDHA, PMAIP1; most repressed include NDUFB8, NDUFA4, ACOX1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Orlistat (phenotype similarity 0.784); nearest-atlas distance 0.216 places Glibenclamide in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Glibenclamide nearest Ixazomib (Proteostasis (proteasome/Hsp90)); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Orlistat (Antidiabetic). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Orlistat directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Metformin, Pioglitazone, Glibenclamide). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism, Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (88%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Skeletal muscle: moderate predicted involvement (51%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as muscle/somite integrity or metabolic load.
The Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.513), reshaping lipid metabolism.
The OXPHOS / mitochondrial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.418), shifting mitochondrial / OXPHOS activity.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Lovastatin) and phenotype anchor (Metformin) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (86%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Orlistat — Antidiabetic
step6_report.mechanism_text: Orlistat (Antidiabetic) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as PGK1, EGLN3, VEGFA; most repressed include ACOX1, FABP4, CPT1A.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Metformin (phenotype similarity 0.862); nearest-atlas distance 0.138 places Orlistat in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Orlistat nearest Lovastatin (Statin); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Metformin (Antidiabetic). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Cyclosporin A directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Pimecrolimus, Tacrolimus, Aspirin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (89%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (53%), driven mainly by the Apoptosis, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.766), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.603), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Romidepsin) and phenotype anchor (Pimecrolimus) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (84%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Cyclosporin A — Immunosuppressant
step6_report.mechanism_text: Cyclosporin A (Immunosuppressant) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BBC3, NDRG1, DGAT1; most repressed include IER3, IRF7, NFKBIA.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Pimecrolimus (phenotype similarity 0.841); nearest-atlas distance 0.159 places Cyclosporin A in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Cyclosporin A nearest Romidepsin (HDAC inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Pimecrolimus (Immunosuppressant). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Tacrolimus directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Pimecrolimus, Leflunomide, Cyclosporin A). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (81%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Vasculature: moderate predicted involvement (48%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.723), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.641), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Pimecrolimus) and phenotype anchor (Pimecrolimus) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (87%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Tacrolimus — Immunosuppressant
step6_report.mechanism_text: Tacrolimus (Immunosuppressant) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as PER1, FKBP5, ACLY; most repressed include CXCL8, RELB, TNF.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Pimecrolimus (phenotype similarity 0.874); nearest-atlas distance 0.126 places Tacrolimus in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Tacrolimus nearest Pimecrolimus (Immunosuppressant); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Pimecrolimus (Immunosuppressant). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Pimecrolimus directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Leflunomide, Tacrolimus, Cyclosporin A). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Interferon / inflammatory, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (78%), driven mainly by the Interferon / inflammatory, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (58%), driven mainly by the Interferon / inflammatory, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.725), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.536), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Tacrolimus) and phenotype anchor (Leflunomide) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (92%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound

step6_report.mechanism_text: Pimecrolimus (Immunosuppressant) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAX, MCL1, BAK1; most repressed include CXCL8, NFKBIA, IFIT3.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Leflunomide directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Pimecrolimus, Tacrolimus, Hydrocortisone). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (64%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (44%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.742), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.596), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Erismodegib) and phenotype anchor (Pimecrolimus) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (92%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Leflunomide — Immunosuppressant
step6_report.mechanism_text: Leflunomide (Immunosuppressant) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as DDIT4, BAX, BID; most repressed include CXCL8, TNF, IL1B.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Pimecrolimus (phenotype similarity 0.921); nearest-atlas distance 0.079 places Leflunomide in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Leflunomide nearest Erismodegib (Hedgehog / Notch); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Pimecrolimus (Immunosuppressant). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Paclitaxel directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Colchicine, Panobinostat, Vinblastine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (99%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Brain / CNS: moderate predicted involvement (44%), driven mainly by the Proteostasis / heat-shock, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.774), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The Apoptosis program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.613), priming cells toward programmed death.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Nifedipine) and phenotype anchor (Colchicine) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (95%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Paclitaxel — Microtubule / cytoskeleton
step6_report.mechanism_text: Paclitaxel (Microtubule / cytoskeleton) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAX, MCL1, PMAIP1; most repressed include CCNB2, UBE2C, MKI67.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Colchicine (phenotype similarity 0.948); nearest-atlas distance 0.052 places Paclitaxel in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Paclitaxel nearest Nifedipine (Ca²⁺ channel blocker); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Colchicine (Microtubule / cytoskeleton). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Vinblastine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Paclitaxel, Colchicine, Epothilone B). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (61%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.812), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.618), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Diltiazem) and phenotype anchor (Paclitaxel) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (90%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Vinblastine — Microtubule / cytoskeleton
step6_report.mechanism_text: Vinblastine (Microtubule / cytoskeleton) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAX, BBC3, BCL2; most repressed include AURKB, PLK1, BIRC5.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Paclitaxel (phenotype similarity 0.896); nearest-atlas distance 0.104 places Vinblastine in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Vinblastine nearest Diltiazem (Ca²⁺ channel blocker); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Paclitaxel (Microtubule / cytoskeleton). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Colchicine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Paclitaxel, Vinblastine, Epothilone B). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (86%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (42%), driven mainly by the Apoptosis, Glucocorticoid / NR response program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.732), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The Apoptosis program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.576), priming cells toward programmed death.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Glibenclamide) and phenotype anchor (Paclitaxel) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (95%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Colchicine — Microtubule / cytoskeleton
step6_report.mechanism_text: Colchicine (Microtubule / cytoskeleton) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BBC3, BAX, CASP3; most repressed include BUB1, MKI67, PCNA.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Paclitaxel (phenotype similarity 0.948); nearest-atlas distance 0.052 places Colchicine in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Colchicine nearest Glibenclamide (Antidiabetic); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Paclitaxel (Microtubule / cytoskeleton). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Epothilone B directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Vinblastine, Mercaptopurine, Romidepsin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (84%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (52%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.837), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.759), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Pimecrolimus) and phenotype anchor (Vinblastine) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (84%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Epothilone B — Microtubule / cytoskeleton
step6_report.mechanism_text: Epothilone B (Microtubule / cytoskeleton) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAX, BBC3, CDKN1A; most repressed include PLK1, UBE2C, CDC20.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Vinblastine (phenotype similarity 0.836); nearest-atlas distance 0.164 places Epothilone B in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Epothilone B nearest Pimecrolimus (Immunosuppressant); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Vinblastine (Microtubule / cytoskeleton). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Resveratrol directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Quercetin, Curcumin, Genistein). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Oxidative stress / NRF2, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (92%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (71%), driven mainly by the Oxidative stress / NRF2 program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The Oxidative stress / NRF2 program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.562), an NRF2 oxidative-stress response.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.421), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Curcumin) and phenotype anchor (Quercetin) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (80%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Resveratrol — Natural product
step6_report.mechanism_text: Resveratrol (Natural product) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as GCLC, NQO1, SLC7A11; most repressed include NFKBIA, CCL2, IL1B.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Quercetin (phenotype similarity 0.801); nearest-atlas distance 0.199 places Resveratrol in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Resveratrol nearest Curcumin (Natural product); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Quercetin (Natural product). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Curcumin directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Quercetin, Genistein, Resveratrol). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (79%), driven mainly by the Oxidative stress / NRF2, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (57%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The Oxidative stress / NRF2 program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.657), an NRF2 oxidative-stress response.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.547), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Resveratrol) and phenotype anchor (Quercetin) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (82%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Curcumin — Natural product
step6_report.mechanism_text: Curcumin (Natural product) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as SRXN1, FTH1, FTL; most repressed include TYMS, NFKBIA, SOD2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Quercetin (phenotype similarity 0.82); nearest-atlas distance 0.18 places Curcumin in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Curcumin nearest Resveratrol (Natural product); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Quercetin (Natural product). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Quercetin directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Curcumin, Resveratrol, Genistein). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Oxidative stress / NRF2, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (86%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (51%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The Oxidative stress / NRF2 program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.556), an NRF2 oxidative-stress response.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.549), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Genistein) and phenotype anchor (Curcumin) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (82%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Quercetin — Natural product
step6_report.mechanism_text: Quercetin (Natural product) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as FTH1, GCLM, TXNRD1; most repressed include CXCL1, IER3, TNF.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Curcumin (phenotype similarity 0.82); nearest-atlas distance 0.18 places Quercetin in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Quercetin nearest Genistein (Natural product); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Curcumin (Natural product). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Genistein directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Curcumin, Quercetin, Resveratrol). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (73%), driven mainly by the Oxidative stress / NRF2, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (65%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, MAPK feedback program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The Oxidative stress / NRF2 program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.691), an NRF2 oxidative-stress response.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.582), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Quercetin) and phenotype anchor (Curcumin) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (80%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Genistein — Natural product
step6_report.mechanism_text: Genistein (Natural product) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as GCLC, TXNRD1, HMOX1; most repressed include RRM2, IER3, TOP2A.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Curcumin (phenotype similarity 0.802); nearest-atlas distance 0.198 places Genistein in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Genistein nearest Quercetin (Natural product); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Curcumin (Natural product). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Olaparib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Rucaparib, Veliparib, Fluorouracil). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (92%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (50%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Senescence / SASP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.901), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.599), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Dinaciclib) and phenotype anchor (Rucaparib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (79%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Olaparib — PARP inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Olaparib (PARP inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as CDKN1A, BBC3, BAX; most repressed include CCND1, HES1, MKI67.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Rucaparib (phenotype similarity 0.794); nearest-atlas distance 0.206 places Olaparib in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Olaparib nearest Dinaciclib (CDK inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Rucaparib (PARP inhibitor). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Rucaparib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Fluorouracil, Niraparib, Gemcitabine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (91%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (38%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.886), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.638), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Sunitinib) and phenotype anchor (Fluorouracil) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (94%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Rucaparib — PARP inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Rucaparib (PARP inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAX, BBC3, CDKN1A; most repressed include MKI67, CDK1, RRM2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Fluorouracil (phenotype similarity 0.944); nearest-atlas distance 0.056 places Rucaparib in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Rucaparib nearest Sunitinib (VEGFR / multi-TKI); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Fluorouracil (Antimetabolite). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Veliparib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Niraparib, Fluorouracil, Rucaparib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (89%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (51%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.92), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.679), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Niraparib) and phenotype anchor (Niraparib) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (92%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Veliparib — PARP inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Veliparib (PARP inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BBC3, SESN2, CDKN1A; most repressed include FOXM1, AURKA, CCNE2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Niraparib (phenotype similarity 0.92); nearest-atlas distance 0.08 places Veliparib in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Veliparib nearest Niraparib (PARP inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Niraparib (PARP inhibitor). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.
