programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Niraparib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Rucaparib, Veliparib, Fluorouracil). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (94%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (56%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.898), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.665), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Veliparib) and phenotype anchor (Rucaparib) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (94%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Niraparib — PARP inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Niraparib (PARP inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAX, CDKN1A, BBC3; most repressed include TOP2A, UBE2C, AURKB.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Rucaparib (phenotype similarity 0.94); nearest-atlas distance 0.06 places Niraparib in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Niraparib nearest Veliparib (PARP inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Rucaparib (PARP inhibitor). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Palbociclib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Ribociclib, Dinaciclib, Roscovitine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (86%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Brain / CNS: moderate predicted involvement (39%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.836), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The Apoptosis program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.431), priming cells toward programmed death.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Ribociclib) and phenotype anchor (Ribociclib) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (83%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Palbociclib — CDK inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Palbociclib (CDK inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as CDKN1A, SESN2, BAX; most repressed include CCNB1, PCNA, AURKA.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Ribociclib (phenotype similarity 0.833); nearest-atlas distance 0.167 places Palbociclib in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Palbociclib nearest Ribociclib (CDK inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Ribociclib (CDK inhibitor). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Ribociclib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Roscovitine, Palbociclib, Dinaciclib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Senescence / SASP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (84%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Brain / CNS: moderate predicted involvement (39%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.812), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The Apoptosis program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.431), priming cells toward programmed death.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Palbociclib) and phenotype anchor (Roscovitine) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (88%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Ribociclib — CDK inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Ribociclib (CDK inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as CDKN1A, CDKN2A, IL6; most repressed include TOP2A, CDK1, RRM2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Roscovitine (phenotype similarity 0.876); nearest-atlas distance 0.124 places Ribociclib in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Ribociclib nearest Palbociclib (CDK inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Roscovitine (CDK inhibitor). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Roscovitine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Ribociclib, Palbociclib, Dinaciclib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Senescence / SASP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (81%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (47%), driven mainly by the Senescence / SASP, Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.829), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The Apoptosis program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.551), priming cells toward programmed death.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Ramipril) and phenotype anchor (Ribociclib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (88%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Roscovitine — CDK inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Roscovitine (CDK inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as CDKN1A, IGFBP3, GLB1; most repressed include CCNA2, CCNE2, CDC20.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Ribociclib (phenotype similarity 0.876); nearest-atlas distance 0.124 places Roscovitine in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Roscovitine nearest Ramipril (RAAS inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Ribociclib (CDK inhibitor). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Gemcitabine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Rucaparib, Fluorouracil, Niraparib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (91%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (58%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.936), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.672), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Dapagliflozin) and phenotype anchor (Rucaparib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (90%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Gemcitabine — Antimetabolite
step6_report.mechanism_text: Gemcitabine (Antimetabolite) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BBC3, BAX, CDKN1A; most repressed include PCNA, CDK1, AURKB.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Rucaparib (phenotype similarity 0.902); nearest-atlas distance 0.098 places Gemcitabine in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Gemcitabine nearest Dapagliflozin (Antidiabetic); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Rucaparib (PARP inhibitor). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Mercaptopurine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Fluorouracil, Rucaparib, Gemcitabine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (93%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (43%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.842), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.679), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Idelalisib) and phenotype anchor (Fluorouracil) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (92%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Mercaptopurine — Antimetabolite
step6_report.mechanism_text: Mercaptopurine (Antimetabolite) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAX, BBC3, SESN2; most repressed include CCNB2, CDC20, FOXM1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Fluorouracil (phenotype similarity 0.917); nearest-atlas distance 0.083 places Mercaptopurine in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Mercaptopurine nearest Idelalisib (PI3K / mTOR); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Fluorouracil (Antimetabolite). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Carfilzomib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Ganetespib, 17-AAG, Vinblastine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Proteostasis / heat-shock, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (97%), driven mainly by the Apoptosis, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (92%), driven mainly by the Proteostasis / heat-shock, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The Proteostasis / heat-shock program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.792), triggering a proteostasis / heat-shock response.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.689), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Enalapril) and phenotype anchor (Ganetespib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (93%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Carfilzomib — Proteostasis (proteasome/Hsp90)
step6_report.mechanism_text: Carfilzomib (Proteostasis (proteasome/Hsp90)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAX, HSPB1, BBC3; most repressed include PLK1, MKI67, PCNA.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Ganetespib (phenotype similarity 0.927); nearest-atlas distance 0.073 places Carfilzomib in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Carfilzomib nearest Enalapril (RAAS inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Ganetespib (Proteostasis (proteasome/Hsp90)). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Ixazomib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Ganetespib, 17-AAG, Paclitaxel). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (84%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (80%), driven mainly by the Proteostasis / heat-shock, Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The Proteostasis / heat-shock program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.771), triggering a proteostasis / heat-shock response.
The Apoptosis program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.67), priming cells toward programmed death.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Glibenclamide) and phenotype anchor (Ganetespib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (82%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Ixazomib — Proteostasis (proteasome/Hsp90)
step6_report.mechanism_text: Ixazomib (Proteostasis (proteasome/Hsp90)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as HSPA1B, HSPA6, HSPB1; most repressed include CCNA2, FOXM1, BIRC5.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Ganetespib (phenotype similarity 0.819); nearest-atlas distance 0.181 places Ixazomib in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Ixazomib nearest Glibenclamide (Antidiabetic); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Ganetespib (Proteostasis (proteasome/Hsp90)). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure 17-AAG directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Ganetespib, Ixazomib, Carfilzomib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Proteostasis / heat-shock, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Apoptosis, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (90%), driven mainly by the Proteostasis / heat-shock, Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The Proteostasis / heat-shock program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.782), triggering a proteostasis / heat-shock response.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.68), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Tacrolimus) and phenotype anchor (Ganetespib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (92%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: 17-AAG — Proteostasis (proteasome/Hsp90)
step6_report.mechanism_text: 17-AAG (Proteostasis (proteasome/Hsp90)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAX, ATF3, BBC3; most repressed include MKI67, TYMS, AURKA.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Ganetespib (phenotype similarity 0.918); nearest-atlas distance 0.082 places 17-AAG in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places 17-AAG nearest Tacrolimus (Immunosuppressant); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Ganetespib (Proteostasis (proteasome/Hsp90)). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Ganetespib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Carfilzomib, 17-AAG, Paclitaxel). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Apoptosis, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (91%), driven mainly by the Apoptosis, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (73%), driven mainly by the Proteostasis / heat-shock, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The Proteostasis / heat-shock program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.793), triggering a proteostasis / heat-shock response.
The Apoptosis program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.662), priming cells toward programmed death.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Celecoxib) and phenotype anchor (Carfilzomib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (93%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Ganetespib — Proteostasis (proteasome/Hsp90)
step6_report.mechanism_text: Ganetespib (Proteostasis (proteasome/Hsp90)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as XBP1, BAX, CRYAB; most repressed include CCNB1, TYMS, CCNE2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Carfilzomib (phenotype similarity 0.927); nearest-atlas distance 0.073 places Ganetespib in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Ganetespib nearest Celecoxib (NSAID); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Carfilzomib (Proteostasis (proteasome/Hsp90)). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Vismodegib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Erismodegib, Avagacestat, DAPT). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Wnt / β-catenin, Notch program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (96%), driven mainly by the Notch, Wnt / β-catenin program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.

Heart: moderate predicted involvement (65%), driven mainly by the Notch, OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.534), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The Notch program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.5), perturbing Notch developmental signalling.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Sorafenib) and phenotype anchor (Erismodegib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (82%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Vismodegib — Hedgehog / Notch
step6_report.mechanism_text: Vismodegib (Hedgehog / Notch) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as ATP5MC1, CXCL1, IER3; most repressed include ASCL2, NOTCH1, CCND1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Erismodegib (phenotype similarity 0.818); nearest-atlas distance 0.182 places Vismodegib in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Vismodegib nearest Sorafenib (VEGFR / multi-TKI); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Erismodegib (Hedgehog / Notch). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Erismodegib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Vismodegib, DAPT, Avagacestat). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Wnt / β-catenin, Notch program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (82%), driven mainly by the Notch, Wnt / β-catenin program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.

Heart: moderate predicted involvement (40%), driven mainly by the Notch program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.
The Translation / ribosome program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.768), throttling protein-synthesis capacity.
The Autophagy / lysosome program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.735), inducing autophagy/lysosomal turnover.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Leflunomide) and phenotype anchor (Vismodegib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (82%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Erismodegib — Hedgehog / Notch
step6_report.mechanism_text: Erismodegib (Hedgehog / Notch) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as FKBP5, STAT1, RPL5; most repressed include DLL1, CCND1, JAG1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Vismodegib (phenotype similarity 0.818); nearest-atlas distance 0.182 places Erismodegib in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Erismodegib nearest Leflunomide (Immunosuppressant); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Vismodegib (Hedgehog / Notch). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure DAPT directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Erismodegib, Vismodegib, Avagacestat). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Wnt / β-catenin, Notch program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (68%), driven mainly by the Notch, Wnt / β-catenin program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.

Blood / immune: moderate predicted involvement (46%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.758), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
The Notch program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.571), perturbing Notch developmental signalling.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Fluoxetine) and phenotype anchor (Erismodegib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (78%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: DAPT — Hedgehog / Notch
step6_report.mechanism_text: DAPT (Hedgehog / Notch) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as MDM2, RRM2B, KLF13; most repressed include NRARP, JAG1, NOTCH1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Erismodegib (phenotype similarity 0.782); nearest-atlas distance 0.218 places DAPT in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places DAPT nearest Fluoxetine (SSRI); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Erismodegib (Hedgehog / Notch). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Avagacestat directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Erismodegib, Vismodegib, DAPT). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Notch, Wnt / β-catenin program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.

Vasculature: strong predicted involvement (94%), driven mainly by the Notch program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (94%), driven mainly by the Notch, Wnt / β-catenin program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The Androgen response program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -1.176), antagonising the androgen-receptor program.
The Notch program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.666), perturbing Notch developmental signalling.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Celecoxib) and phenotype anchor (Erismodegib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (76%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

narrative: We don't measure Propranolol directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Metoprolol, Dapagliflozin, Pioglitazone). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (78%), driven mainly by the Hypoxia, Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (70%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.
The Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.467), reshaping lipid metabolism.
The OXPHOS / mitochondrial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.399), shifting mitochondrial / OXPHOS activity.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Metoprolol) and phenotype anchor (Metoprolol) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (61%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Metoprolol directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Atenolol, Orlistat, Propranolol). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Hypoxia, OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (77%), driven mainly by the Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Brain / CNS: moderate predicted involvement (58%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.459), reshaping lipid metabolism.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.371), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Atenolol) and phenotype anchor (Atenolol) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (70%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Metoprolol — β-adrenergic
step6_report.mechanism_text: Metoprolol (β-adrenergic) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as PGK1, ADM, SLC2A1; most repressed include ACOX1, ELOVL6, SCD.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Atenolol (phenotype similarity 0.696); nearest-atlas distance 0.304 places Metoprolol in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Metoprolol nearest Atenolol (β-adrenergic); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Atenolol (β-adrenergic). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Diphenhydramine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Resveratrol, Famotidine, Ibuprofen). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (93%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (80%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The Oxidative stress / NRF2 program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.683), an NRF2 oxidative-stress response.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.619), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Fluoxetine) and phenotype anchor (Resveratrol) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (50%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Diphenhydramine — Histamine (H1/H2)
step6_report.mechanism_text: Diphenhydramine (Histamine (H1/H2)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as CCND1, NOTCH1, KDR; most repressed include CXCL8, TNF, CCL2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Resveratrol (phenotype similarity 0.498); nearest-atlas distance 0.502 places Diphenhydramine in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Diphenhydramine nearest Fluoxetine (SSRI); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Resveratrol (Natural product). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Loratadine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Aspirin, Ibuprofen, Leflunomide). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (66%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Vasculature: moderate predicted involvement (59%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.792), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.47), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Clozapine) and phenotype anchor (Aspirin) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (75%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Loratadine — Histamine (H1/H2)
step6_report.mechanism_text: Loratadine (Histamine (H1/H2)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as IGFBP3, EIF4EBP1, GABARAPL1; most repressed include CXCL1, NFKBIA, SOD2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Aspirin (phenotype similarity 0.747); nearest-atlas distance 0.253 places Loratadine in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Loratadine nearest Clozapine (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Aspirin (NSAID). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Famotidine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Leflunomide, Ibuprofen, Loratadine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (99%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Vasculature: strong predicted involvement (99%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.764), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.447), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Avagacestat) and phenotype anchor (Leflunomide) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (54%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Famotidine — Histamine (H1/H2)
step6_report.mechanism_text: Famotidine (Histamine (H1/H2)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as FDPS, HEY1, TWIST1; most repressed include SOD2, TNFAIP3, RELB.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Leflunomide (phenotype similarity 0.544); nearest-atlas distance 0.456 places Famotidine in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Famotidine nearest Avagacestat (Hedgehog / Notch); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Leflunomide (Immunosuppressant). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Nifedipine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Sorafenib, Fluoxetine, Axitinib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Vasculature: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Hypoxia, Angiogenesis / endothelial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (96%), driven mainly by the Hypoxia, OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (71%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The Angiogenesis / endothelial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.68), consistent with an anti-angiogenic action.
The MAPK feedback program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.464), reflecting MAPK-pathway feedback.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Amlodipine) and phenotype anchor (Sorafenib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (64%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Nifedipine — Ca²⁺ channel blocker
step6_report.mechanism_text: Nifedipine (Ca²⁺ channel blocker) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as LDHA, BNIP3, SQSTM1; most repressed include NDUFA4, SPRY4, KDR.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Sorafenib (phenotype similarity 0.638); nearest-atlas distance 0.362 places Nifedipine in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Nifedipine nearest Amlodipine (Ca²⁺ channel blocker); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Sorafenib (VEGFR / multi-TKI). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Amlodipine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Resveratrol, Verapamil, Haloperidol). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (93%), driven mainly by the Oxidative stress / NRF2 program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (84%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.
The Oxidative stress / NRF2 program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.679), an NRF2 oxidative-stress response.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.459), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Nifedipine) and phenotype anchor (Resveratrol) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (53%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Amlodipine — Ca²⁺ channel blocker
step6_report.mechanism_text: Amlodipine (Ca²⁺ channel blocker) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as FTH1, BAK1, NQO1; most repressed include MRPL13, NDUFA4, UQCRC2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Resveratrol (phenotype similarity 0.531); nearest-atlas distance 0.469 places Amlodipine in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Amlodipine nearest Nifedipine (Ca²⁺ channel blocker); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Resveratrol (Natural product). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Verapamil directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Metoprolol, Amlodipine, Lidocaine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (82%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.

Skeletal muscle: moderate predicted involvement (59%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as muscle/somite integrity or metabolic load.
The Proteostasis / heat-shock program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.363), triggering a proteostasis / heat-shock response.
The Hypoxia program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.289), suggesting a hypoxia-like stress response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Dofetilide) and phenotype anchor (Metoprolol) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (45%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Verapamil — Ca²⁺ channel blocker
step6_report.mechanism_text: Verapamil (Ca²⁺ channel blocker) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BNIP3, SLC2A1, EIF4EBP1; most repressed include HES1, MRPL13, NDUFB8.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Metoprolol (phenotype similarity 0.451); nearest-atlas distance 0.549 places Verapamil in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Verapamil nearest Dofetilide (Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Metoprolol (β-adrenergic). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Diltiazem directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Metformin, Ticagrelor, Dapagliflozin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (70%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (67%), driven mainly by the Oxidative stress / NRF2, OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The Autophagy / lysosome program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.455), inducing autophagy/lysosomal turnover.
The OXPHOS / mitochondrial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.373), shifting mitochondrial / OXPHOS activity.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Diphenhydramine) and phenotype anchor (Metformin) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (46%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Diltiazem — Ca²⁺ channel blocker
step6_report.mechanism_text: Diltiazem (Ca²⁺ channel blocker) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as PGK1, NDRG1, PDK1; most repressed include UQCRC2, NDUFA4, COX6C.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Metformin (phenotype similarity 0.465); nearest-atlas distance 0.535 places Diltiazem in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Diltiazem nearest Diphenhydramine (Histamine (H1/H2)); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Metformin (Antidiabetic). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Lidocaine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Isoprenaline, Clozapine, Paroxetine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Proteostasis / heat-shock program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Skeletal muscle: strong predicted involvement (94%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Proteostasis / heat-shock program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as muscle/somite integrity or metabolic load.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (88%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Proteostasis / heat-shock program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The Autophagy / lysosome program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.38), inducing autophagy/lysosomal turnover.
The Cholesterol / SREBP program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.361), engaging the cholesterol-biosynthesis feedback axis.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Vorinostat) and phenotype anchor (Isoprenaline) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (50%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Lidocaine — Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator
step6_report.mechanism_text: Lidocaine (Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as EIF4EBP1, HSPA1B, DDIT3; most repressed include COX6C, NDUFA4, UQCRC2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Isoprenaline (phenotype similarity 0.497); nearest-atlas distance 0.503 places Lidocaine in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Lidocaine nearest Vorinostat (HDAC inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Isoprenaline (β-adrenergic). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.
