programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Carbamazepine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Dofetilide, Isoprenaline, Amiodarone). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Heart: moderate predicted involvement (58%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Vasculature: moderate predicted involvement (54%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.
The Cholesterol / SREBP program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.913), engaging the cholesterol-biosynthesis feedback axis.
The Oxidative stress / NRF2 program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.36), an NRF2 oxidative-stress response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Aspirin) and phenotype anchor (Dofetilide) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (48%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Carbamazepine — Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator
step6_report.mechanism_text: Carbamazepine (Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as MSMO1, SERPINE1, SREBF2; most repressed include ETV5, PHLDA1, SPRY2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Dofetilide (phenotype similarity 0.478); nearest-atlas distance 0.522 places Carbamazepine in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Carbamazepine nearest Aspirin (NSAID); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Dofetilide (Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Amiodarone directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Clopidogrel, Dofetilide, Metoprolol). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Oxidative stress / NRF2 program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (68%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (61%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.527), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.443), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Lidocaine) and phenotype anchor (Clopidogrel) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (62%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Amiodarone — Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator
step6_report.mechanism_text: Amiodarone (Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as GCLM, MDM2, NQO1; most repressed include PER1, WIPI1, GABARAPL1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Clopidogrel (phenotype similarity 0.625); nearest-atlas distance 0.375 places Amiodarone in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Amiodarone nearest Lidocaine (Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Clopidogrel (Coagulation / platelets). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Dofetilide directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Amiodarone, Carbamazepine, Citalopram). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Oxidative stress / NRF2, OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (71%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Oxidative stress / NRF2 program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Brain / CNS: moderate predicted involvement (63%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial, Oxidative stress / NRF2 program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The Androgen response program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.285), antagonising the androgen-receptor program.
The MAPK feedback program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.283), reflecting MAPK-pathway feedback.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Metoprolol) and phenotype anchor (Amiodarone) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (48%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Dofetilide — Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator
step6_report.mechanism_text: Dofetilide (Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as HMOX1, GCLC, SRXN1; most repressed include COX6C, NDUFB8, UQCRC2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Amiodarone (phenotype similarity 0.485); nearest-atlas distance 0.515 places Dofetilide in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Dofetilide nearest Metoprolol (β-adrenergic); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Amiodarone (Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Enzalutamide directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Abiraterone, Bicalutamide, Finasteride). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (95%), driven mainly by the Androgen response program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (80%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The Androgen response program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.806), antagonising the androgen-receptor program.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.623), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Bicalutamide) and phenotype anchor (Abiraterone) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (79%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Enzalutamide — Androgen axis
step6_report.mechanism_text: Enzalutamide (Androgen axis) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BCL2L11, BAK1, CASP3; most repressed include NKX3-1, FKBP5, TMPRSS2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Abiraterone (phenotype similarity 0.792); nearest-atlas distance 0.208 places Enzalutamide in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Enzalutamide nearest Bicalutamide (Androgen axis); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Abiraterone (Androgen axis). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Bicalutamide directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Finasteride, Abiraterone, Enzalutamide). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (97%), driven mainly by the Androgen response, Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (79%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The Androgen response program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.714), antagonising the androgen-receptor program.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.588), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Enzalutamide) and phenotype anchor (Finasteride) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (85%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Bicalutamide — Androgen axis
step6_report.mechanism_text: Bicalutamide (Androgen axis) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BCL2, DDIT4, BAK1; most repressed include STEAP4, TMPRSS2, NDRG1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Finasteride (phenotype similarity 0.846); nearest-atlas distance 0.154 places Bicalutamide in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Bicalutamide nearest Enzalutamide (Androgen axis); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Finasteride (Androgen axis). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Finasteride directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Bicalutamide, Enzalutamide, Abiraterone). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Androgen response, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (87%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (87%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.
The Androgen response program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.701), antagonising the androgen-receptor program.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.511), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Prednisone) and phenotype anchor (Bicalutamide) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (85%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Finasteride — Androgen axis
step6_report.mechanism_text: Finasteride (Androgen axis) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BBC3, BAX, NRP1; most repressed include STEAP4, ABCC4, NKX3-1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Bicalutamide (phenotype similarity 0.846); nearest-atlas distance 0.154 places Finasteride in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Finasteride nearest Prednisone (Glucocorticoid); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Bicalutamide (Androgen axis). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Abiraterone directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Bicalutamide, Enzalutamide, Finasteride). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Androgen response program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (80%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (67%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.
The Androgen response program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.818), antagonising the androgen-receptor program.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.628), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Hydrocortisone) and phenotype anchor (Bicalutamide) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (79%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Abiraterone — Androgen axis
step6_report.mechanism_text: Abiraterone (Androgen axis) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as CA12, GREB1, IGFBP4; most repressed include NKX3-1, KLK2, ABCC4.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Bicalutamide (phenotype similarity 0.792); nearest-atlas distance 0.208 places Abiraterone in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Abiraterone nearest Hydrocortisone (Glucocorticoid); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Bicalutamide (Androgen axis). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Rivaroxaban directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Losartan, Ticagrelor, Nifedipine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Vasculature: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Blood / immune: moderate predicted involvement (65%), driven mainly by the Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Heart: moderate predicted involvement (58%), driven mainly by the Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.45), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Estrogen response program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.328), a coordinated transcriptional shift.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Apixaban) and phenotype anchor (Losartan) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (47%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Rivaroxaban — Coagulation / platelets
step6_report.mechanism_text: Rivaroxaban (Coagulation / platelets) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as PDK1, IL6, ADM; most repressed include FN1, TEK, SNAI2.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Losartan (phenotype similarity 0.473); nearest-atlas distance 0.527 places Rivaroxaban in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Rivaroxaban nearest Apixaban (Coagulation / platelets); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Losartan (RAAS inhibitor). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Apixaban directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Ramipril, Sunitinib, Axitinib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (64%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Blood / immune: moderate predicted involvement (62%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.
The Angiogenesis / endothelial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.664), consistent with an anti-angiogenic action.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.624), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Diltiazem) and phenotype anchor (Ramipril) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (47%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Apixaban — Coagulation / platelets
step6_report.mechanism_text: Apixaban (Coagulation / platelets) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as NCL, BAK1, RPL11; most repressed include PECAM1, ESM1, FDFT1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Ramipril (phenotype similarity 0.467); nearest-atlas distance 0.533 places Apixaban in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Apixaban nearest Diltiazem (Ca²⁺ channel blocker); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Ramipril (RAAS inhibitor). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Clopidogrel directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Amiodarone, Valsartan, Dofetilide). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Brain / CNS: moderate predicted involvement (56%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.

Heart: moderate predicted involvement (52%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.475), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Hypoxia program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.315), suggesting a hypoxia-like stress response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Amlodipine) and phenotype anchor (Amiodarone) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (62%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Clopidogrel — Coagulation / platelets
step6_report.mechanism_text: Clopidogrel (Coagulation / platelets) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as OSGIN1, FTH1, SLC7A11; most repressed include BCL2, CASP3, TFF1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Amiodarone (phenotype similarity 0.625); nearest-atlas distance 0.375 places Clopidogrel in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Clopidogrel nearest Amlodipine (Ca²⁺ channel blocker); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Amiodarone (Na⁺/K⁺ channel modulator). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Ticagrelor directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Valsartan, Losartan, Diltiazem). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Hypoxia, OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Vasculature: strong predicted involvement (90%), driven mainly by the Hypoxia, Notch program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (89%), driven mainly by the Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.528), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Estrogen response program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.328), a coordinated transcriptional shift.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Dinaciclib) and phenotype anchor (Valsartan) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (62%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Ticagrelor — Coagulation / platelets
step6_report.mechanism_text: Ticagrelor (Coagulation / platelets) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as NDRG1, LDHA, SLC2A1; most repressed include SOD2, GCLC, COX5A.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Valsartan (phenotype similarity 0.616); nearest-atlas distance 0.384 places Ticagrelor in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Ticagrelor nearest Dinaciclib (CDK inhibitor); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Valsartan (RAAS inhibitor). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Haloperidol directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Lovastatin, Atorvastatin, Simvastatin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP, Fatty-acid / lipid metabolism program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Vasculature: moderate predicted involvement (44%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Kidney (pronephros): moderate predicted involvement (42%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as pronephros filtration or fluid-balance effects.
The Cholesterol / SREBP program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.794), engaging the cholesterol-biosynthesis feedback axis.
The Autophagy / lysosome program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.405), inducing autophagy/lysosomal turnover.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Aripiprazole) and phenotype anchor (Lovastatin) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (57%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Haloperidol — Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)
step6_report.mechanism_text: Haloperidol (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as NKX3-1, TMPRSS2, ABCC4; most repressed include SDHB, INSR, VEGFA.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Lovastatin (phenotype similarity 0.573); nearest-atlas distance 0.427 places Haloperidol in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Haloperidol nearest Aripiprazole (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Lovastatin (Statin). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Clozapine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Aripiprazole, Citalopram, Fluoxetine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP, Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Vasculature: moderate predicted involvement (48%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Heart: moderate predicted involvement (38%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.
The Cholesterol / SREBP program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.644), engaging the cholesterol-biosynthesis feedback axis.
The Autophagy / lysosome program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.383), inducing autophagy/lysosomal turnover.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Olanzapine) and phenotype anchor (Aripiprazole) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (72%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Clozapine — Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)
step6_report.mechanism_text: Clozapine (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as LDLR, WIPI1, SQLE; most repressed include FN1, VIM, COL1A1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Aripiprazole (phenotype similarity 0.715); nearest-atlas distance 0.285 places Clozapine in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Clozapine nearest Olanzapine (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Aripiprazole (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Olanzapine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Citalopram, Pravastatin, Atorvastatin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP, Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Kidney (pronephros): moderate predicted involvement (41%), driven mainly by the Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as pronephros filtration or fluid-balance effects.

Skeletal muscle: moderate predicted involvement (37%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as muscle/somite integrity or metabolic load.
The Cholesterol / SREBP program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.598), engaging the cholesterol-biosynthesis feedback axis.
The Autophagy / lysosome program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.4), inducing autophagy/lysosomal turnover.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Clozapine) and phenotype anchor (Citalopram) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (59%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Olanzapine — Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)
step6_report.mechanism_text: Olanzapine (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as INSIG1, DHCR7, FDFT1; most repressed include KLK3, STEAP4, ABCC4.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Citalopram (phenotype similarity 0.593); nearest-atlas distance 0.407 places Olanzapine in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Olanzapine nearest Clozapine (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Citalopram (SSRI). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Aripiprazole directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Clozapine, Citalopram, Pravastatin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cholesterol / SREBP, Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Brain / CNS: moderate predicted involvement (54%), driven mainly by the Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.

Skeletal muscle: moderate predicted involvement (43%), driven mainly by the several shared programs program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as muscle/somite integrity or metabolic load.
The Cholesterol / SREBP program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.612), engaging the cholesterol-biosynthesis feedback axis.
The Autophagy / lysosome program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.382), inducing autophagy/lysosomal turnover.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Clozapine) and phenotype anchor (Clozapine) point the same way, so this inference is high-confidence (72%).
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Aripiprazole — Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)
step6_report.mechanism_text: Aripiprazole (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with a synthesized whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as HMGCS1, SQSTM1, IDI1; most repressed include AXIN2, NKD1, TCF7.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Clozapine (phenotype similarity 0.715); nearest-atlas distance 0.285 places Aripiprazole in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Aripiprazole nearest Clozapine (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)); its synthesized phenotype places it nearest Clozapine (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)). The two routes agree.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Imatinib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Sunitinib, Palbociclib, Vinblastine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, MAPK feedback program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (98%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, MAPK feedback program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Vasculature: moderate predicted involvement (53%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, MAPK feedback program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.
The Angiogenesis / endothelial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.808), consistent with an anti-angiogenic action.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.801), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Entinostat) and phenotype anchor (Sunitinib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (67%).
Because this compound has published literature, the research dossier (Step 1) further constrains the read — in production those findings reweight the neighbor consensus before we screen.
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Imatinib — Kinase inhibitor (BCR-ABL/KIT)
step6_report.mechanism_text: Imatinib (Kinase inhibitor (BCR-ABL/KIT)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with an interpolated whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BBC3, BAX, MCL1; most repressed include MKI67, UBE2C, CDK1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Sunitinib (phenotype similarity 0.673); nearest-atlas distance 0.327 places Imatinib in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Imatinib nearest Entinostat (HDAC inhibitor); its interpolated phenotype places it nearest Sunitinib (VEGFR / multi-TKI). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

dossier.moa: Competitive ATP-site tyrosine-kinase inhibitor; locks BCR-ABL in an inactive conformation.
findings: First-in-class targeted kinase inhibitor (Gleevec); transformed CML to a chronic condition.
Off-target KIT/PDGFR activity extends use to GIST and other tumours.
Cardiac and fluid-retention signals reported on long-term therapy.
dossier.zebrafish: Zebrafish kdr/kit models recapitulate vascular and pigment-cell effects of KIT/PDGFR blockade.
dossier.source: illustrative literature dossier (in production: live agentic literature search)

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Gefitinib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Vinblastine, Sorafenib, Apixaban). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the MAPK feedback, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (88%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, MAPK feedback program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (70%), driven mainly by the PI3K–AKT–mTOR, Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The Angiogenesis / endothelial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.621), consistent with an anti-angiogenic action.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.59), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Aripiprazole) and phenotype anchor (Vinblastine) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (48%).
Because this compound has published literature, the research dossier (Step 1) further constrains the read — in production those findings reweight the neighbor consensus before we screen.
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Gefitinib — EGFR inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Gefitinib (EGFR inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with an interpolated whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAK1, BCL2, CASP3; most repressed include DUSP4, SPRY2, PHLDA1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Vinblastine (phenotype similarity 0.479); nearest-atlas distance 0.521 places Gefitinib in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Gefitinib nearest Aripiprazole (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)); its interpolated phenotype places it nearest Vinblastine (Microtubule / cytoskeleton). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

dossier.moa: Reversible EGFR tyrosine-kinase inhibitor; blocks downstream MAPK/PI3K signalling.
findings: Dramatic responses in EGFR exon-19/L858R mutant lung cancer.
Acquired T790M resistance limits durability.
Class-typical rash and diarrhoea reflect EGFR's role in skin and gut.
dossier.zebrafish: egfra morphants show epidermal and fin-fold defects mirroring on-target toxicity.
dossier.source: illustrative literature dossier (in production: live agentic literature search)

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Erlotinib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Axitinib, Pazopanib, Sunitinib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the MAPK feedback, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (86%), driven mainly by the MAPK feedback, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (53%), driven mainly by the PI3K–AKT–mTOR program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The Angiogenesis / endothelial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.624), consistent with an anti-angiogenic action.
The PI3K–AKT–mTOR program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.43), tuning the PI3K–AKT–mTOR growth axis.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Metoprolol) and phenotype anchor (Axitinib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (49%).
Because this compound has published literature, the research dossier (Step 1) further constrains the read — in production those findings reweight the neighbor consensus before we screen.
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Erlotinib — EGFR inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Erlotinib (EGFR inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with an interpolated whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as KLK3, TWIST1, NDRG1; most repressed include EPHA2, SESN2, PHLDA1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Axitinib (phenotype similarity 0.493); nearest-atlas distance 0.507 places Erlotinib in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Erlotinib nearest Metoprolol (β-adrenergic); its interpolated phenotype places it nearest Axitinib (VEGFR / multi-TKI). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

findings: Survival benefit in NSCLC and (with gemcitabine) pancreatic cancer.
Rash severity correlates with response.
Shares EGFR-blockade liabilities with gefitinib.
dossier.zebrafish: Shared EGFR axis makes zebrafish epidermal readouts informative.
dossier.source: illustrative literature dossier (in production: live agentic literature search)

narrative: We don't measure Doxorubicin directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Rucaparib, Niraparib, Gemcitabine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (83%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (71%), driven mainly by the p53 / DNA-damage, Oxidative stress / NRF2 program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.92), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.679), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Budesonide) and phenotype anchor (Rucaparib) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (88%).
Because this compound has published literature, the research dossier (Step 1) further constrains the read — in production those findings reweight the neighbor consensus before we screen.
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Doxorubicin — Topoisomerase-II / anthracycline
step6_report.mechanism_text: Doxorubicin (Topoisomerase-II / anthracycline) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with an interpolated whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BBC3, BAX, CDKN1A; most repressed include AURKA, CCNB1, PCNA.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Rucaparib (phenotype similarity 0.885); nearest-atlas distance 0.115 places Doxorubicin in the in-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Doxorubicin nearest Budesonide (Glucocorticoid); its interpolated phenotype places it nearest Rucaparib (PARP inhibitor). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

dossier.moa: Intercalates DNA and poisons topoisomerase-II, causing double-strand breaks; generates ROS.
findings: Backbone chemotherapeutic across many cancers.
Dose-limiting, cumulative cardiotoxicity.
Strong DNA-damage/p53 transcriptional response.
dossier.zebrafish: A validated zebrafish cardiotoxicity model — doxorubicin reduces ventricular function and is used to screen cardioprotectants.
dossier.source: illustrative literature dossier (in production: live agentic literature search)

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Methotrexate directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Vinblastine, Fluorouracil, Niraparib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (98%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, p53 / DNA-damage program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Brain / CNS: moderate predicted involvement (50%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.801), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The p53 / DNA-damage program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.755), a DNA-damage / tumour-suppressor response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Entinostat) and phenotype anchor (Vinblastine) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (86%).
Because this compound has published literature, the research dossier (Step 1) further constrains the read — in production those findings reweight the neighbor consensus before we screen.
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Methotrexate — Antifolate (DHFR)
step6_report.mechanism_text: Methotrexate (Antifolate (DHFR)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with an interpolated whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BAX, BBC3, GADD45A; most repressed include AURKB, CDK1, BUB1.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Vinblastine (phenotype similarity 0.86); nearest-atlas distance 0.14 places Methotrexate in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Methotrexate nearest Entinostat (HDAC inhibitor); its interpolated phenotype places it nearest Vinblastine (Microtubule / cytoskeleton). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

dossier.moa: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, depleting reduced folates and blocking nucleotide synthesis.
findings: Antiproliferative in cancer and immunomodulatory at low dose.
Hepatotoxicity and myelosuppression are key liabilities.
Folate rescue mitigates high-dose toxicity.
dossier.zebrafish: dhfr knockdown phenocopies folate-deficiency developmental defects.
dossier.source: illustrative literature dossier (in production: live agentic literature search)

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Tamoxifen directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Haloperidol, Carbamazepine, Apixaban). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Estrogen response program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (70%), driven mainly by the Estrogen response, OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (68%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.784), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.563), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Diphenhydramine) and phenotype anchor (Haloperidol) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (49%).
Because this compound has published literature, the research dossier (Step 1) further constrains the read — in production those findings reweight the neighbor consensus before we screen.
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Tamoxifen — Estrogen-receptor modulator
step6_report.mechanism_text: Tamoxifen (Estrogen-receptor modulator) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with an interpolated whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as CASP3, BBC3, SOD2; most repressed include CCND1, PGR, MYB.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Haloperidol (phenotype similarity 0.49); nearest-atlas distance 0.51 places Tamoxifen in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Tamoxifen nearest Diphenhydramine (Histamine (H1/H2)); its interpolated phenotype places it nearest Haloperidol (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

dossier.moa: Selective estrogen-receptor modulator; antagonist in breast, partial agonist elsewhere.
findings: Cornerstone of ER+ breast-cancer therapy and prevention.
Endometrial-agonist activity raises uterine risk.
Active metabolite endoxifen drives effect.
dossier.zebrafish: Widely used as the inducer for ERT2/Cre lineage tracing; also an estrogenic endocrine readout.
dossier.source: illustrative literature dossier (in production: live agentic literature search)

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Warfarin directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Quercetin, Curcumin, Resveratrol). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Oxidative stress / NRF2, Cholesterol / SREBP program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (66%), driven mainly by the Apoptosis, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Heart: moderate predicted involvement (61%), driven mainly by the OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.
The Oxidative stress / NRF2 program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.661), an NRF2 oxidative-stress response.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.413), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Aspirin) and phenotype anchor (Quercetin) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (74%).
Because this compound has published literature, the research dossier (Step 1) further constrains the read — in production those findings reweight the neighbor consensus before we screen.
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Warfarin — Vitamin-K antagonist
step6_report.mechanism_text: Warfarin (Vitamin-K antagonist) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with an interpolated whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as SERPINE1, BAX, COX6C; most repressed include CCL2, PECAM1, DDIT4.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Quercetin (phenotype similarity 0.743); nearest-atlas distance 0.257 places Warfarin in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Warfarin nearest Aspirin (NSAID); its interpolated phenotype places it nearest Quercetin (Natural product). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

dossier.moa: Inhibits vitamin-K epoxide reductase, lowering functional clotting factors II/VII/IX/X.
findings: Narrow therapeutic index; CYP2C9/VKORC1 pharmacogenetics matter.
Teratogenic — fetal warfarin syndrome.
Bleeding is the dominant toxicity.
dossier.zebrafish: vkorc1 and coagulation-factor models make zebrafish a haemostasis screen.
dossier.source: illustrative literature dossier (in production: live agentic literature search)
