programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Sildenafil directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Loratadine, Leflunomide, Erismodegib). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Vasculature: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as angiogenesis and vessel-patterning changes.

Heart: strong predicted involvement (71%), driven mainly by the Angiogenesis / endothelial, Hypoxia program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as shifts in heart rate, contractility, or cardiac-stress markers.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (70%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.
The Notch program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.714), perturbing Notch developmental signalling.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.686), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Clozapine) and phenotype anchor (Loratadine) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (31%).
Because this compound has published literature, the research dossier (Step 1) further constrains the read — in production those findings reweight the neighbor consensus before we screen.
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Sildenafil — PDE5 inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Sildenafil (PDE5 inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with an interpolated whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as ANGPT2, TEK, FLT1; most repressed include BIRC3, BBC3, TNFAIP3.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Loratadine (phenotype similarity 0.306); nearest-atlas distance 0.694 places Sildenafil in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Sildenafil nearest Clozapine (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)); its interpolated phenotype places it nearest Loratadine (Histamine (H1/H2)). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

dossier.moa: Inhibits phosphodiesterase-5, raising cGMP and relaxing vascular smooth muscle.
findings: Repurposed from angina to ED to PAH.
Vasodilatory and visual side effects (PDE6 cross-talk).
Pro-angiogenic in some contexts.
dossier.zebrafish: Affects vascular tone and is used in zebrafish cardiovascular assays.
dossier.source: illustrative literature dossier (in production: live agentic literature search)

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Omeprazole directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Fluoxetine, Nifedipine, Paroxetine). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Autophagy / lysosome, Oxidative stress / NRF2 program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.

Kidney (pronephros): strong predicted involvement (88%), driven mainly by the Autophagy / lysosome program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as pronephros filtration or fluid-balance effects.
The Autophagy / lysosome program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.31), inducing autophagy/lysosomal turnover.
The Cholesterol / SREBP program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.306), engaging the cholesterol-biosynthesis feedback axis.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Pioglitazone) and phenotype anchor (Fluoxetine) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (50%).
Because this compound has published literature, the research dossier (Step 1) further constrains the read — in production those findings reweight the neighbor consensus before we screen.
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Omeprazole — Proton-pump inhibitor
step6_report.mechanism_text: Omeprazole (Proton-pump inhibitor) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with an interpolated whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as LAMP1, GABARAPL1, MAP1LC3B; most repressed include CCND1, TCF7, RNF43.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Fluoxetine (phenotype similarity 0.498); nearest-atlas distance 0.502 places Omeprazole in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Omeprazole nearest Pioglitazone (Antidiabetic); its interpolated phenotype places it nearest Fluoxetine (SSRI). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

dossier.moa: Irreversibly inhibits the gastric proton pump.
findings: Very widely used; generally well tolerated.
Long-term use linked to micronutrient and renal signals.
CYP2C19 metabolism drives variability.
dossier.zebrafish: atp4a models inform gastric-acid and ionocyte biology.
dossier.source: illustrative literature dossier (in production: live agentic literature search)

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Morphine directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Loratadine, Paroxetine, Resveratrol). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Liver: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Autophagy / lysosome, NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.

Brain / CNS: strong predicted involvement (81%), driven mainly by the Autophagy / lysosome, OXPHOS / mitochondrial program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as altered neural-activity or neurotoxicity readouts.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (78%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.582), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Oxidative stress / NRF2 program is consistently induced across these neighbors (consensus +0.486), an NRF2 oxidative-stress response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Aripiprazole) and phenotype anchor (Loratadine) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (58%).
Because this compound has published literature, the research dossier (Step 1) further constrains the read — in production those findings reweight the neighbor consensus before we screen.
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Morphine — Opioid agonist
step6_report.mechanism_text: Morphine (Opioid agonist) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with an interpolated whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as SQSTM1, MAP1LC3B, LAMP1; most repressed include CCL2, ATP5F1A, BIRC3.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Loratadine (phenotype similarity 0.585); nearest-atlas distance 0.415 places Morphine in the out-of-domain band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Morphine nearest Aripiprazole (Antipsychotic (dopaminergic)); its interpolated phenotype places it nearest Loratadine (Histamine (H1/H2)). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

dossier.moa: μ-opioid receptor agonist; inhibits ascending pain transmission.
findings: Gold-standard analgesic with tolerance/dependence liabilities.
Respiratory depression is the lethal toxicity.
CNS-dominant pharmacology.
dossier.zebrafish: oprm1 zebrafish show conserved analgesic and reward behaviours used in addiction screens.
dossier.source: illustrative literature dossier (in production: live agentic literature search)

programs.basis: signature score = synthesized mean log2FC of canonical marker genes for the drug's class (illustrative; not measured)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

step3_embedding.chem_projection: PCA(2) of 94-compound standardized RDKit descriptor space

why.basis: genes moved the same direction in both (synthesized)

narrative: We don't measure Diclofenac directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Leflunomide, Pimecrolimus, Aspirin). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: moderate predicted involvement (60%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Apoptosis program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Liver: moderate predicted involvement (56%), driven mainly by the NF-κB / TNF inflammatory, Interferon / inflammatory program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as hepatic metabolism, lipid handling, or clearance effects.
The NF-κB / TNF inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.776), damping NF-κB inflammatory signalling.
The Interferon / inflammatory program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.595), modulating the interferon response.
Confidence: its chemistry anchor (Vorinostat) and phenotype anchor (Leflunomide) diverge, so this inference is moderate-confidence (83%).
Because this compound has published literature, the research dossier (Step 1) further constrains the read — in production those findings reweight the neighbor consensus before we screen.
This interpretation layer is the payoff: it turns an abstract atlas location into concrete, organ- and pathway-level hypotheses you can take straight to a wet-lab zebrafish screen.
neighbor_effects.basis: the candidate inherits the consensus effect of its nearest atlas neighbors; organ involvement is illustrative, a stand-in for the whole-organism zebrafish readout

step5_reliability.metric: 1 − phenotype cosine similarity to nearest atlas compound
step5_reliability.basis: 94-compound MegaFin atlas; tertile bands p33=0.139 p66=0.247

step6_report.headline: Diclofenac — NSAID (COX)
step6_report.mechanism_text: Diclofenac (NSAID (COX)) is placed in the MegaFin atlas with an interpolated whole-organism response (illustrative). Its top induced programs drive genes such as BCL2, CCND1, ASCL2; most repressed include IER3, TNF, BIRC3.
step6_report.confidence_text: Nearest atlas neighbor is Leflunomide (phenotype similarity 0.831); nearest-atlas distance 0.169 places Diclofenac in the near-edge band of the 94-compound manifold.
step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Diclofenac nearest Vorinostat (HDAC inhibitor); its interpolated phenotype places it nearest Leflunomide (Immunosuppressant). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.

dossier.moa: Non-selective cyclo-oxygenase inhibitor; blocks prostaglandin synthesis.
findings: Potent anti-inflammatory/analgesic.
GI and cardiovascular risk class-typical of NSAIDs.
A notable aquatic eco-toxicant — renal/gill effects in fish.
dossier.zebrafish: A classic zebrafish eco-tox model — diclofenac causes pronephros and yolk-edema phenotypes.
dossier.source: illustrative literature dossier (in production: live agentic literature search)

step2_fingerprint.organ_basis: illustrative zebrafish organ-system involvement inferred from the synthesized programs via a curated pathway→organ map; a stand-in for real MegaFin data

narrative: We don't measure Trametinib directly — we read its likely whole-organism effect from its nearest characterized atlas neighbors (Mercaptopurine, Colchicine, Paclitaxel). Everything below is that interpolated consensus.

Blood / immune: strong predicted involvement (100%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, MAPK feedback program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as haematopoietic or inflammatory shifts.

Intestine / gut: strong predicted involvement (95%), driven mainly by the Cell cycle / E2F–G2M, MAPK feedback program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as effects on the rapidly-dividing gut epithelium.

Eye / retina: moderate predicted involvement (45%), driven mainly by the MAPK feedback, Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program(s) shared with its neighbors — in a zebrafish screen this would likely surface as changes in eye development or retinal markers.
The Cell cycle / E2F–G2M program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.914), pointing to anti-proliferative pressure.
The Angiogenesis / endothelial program is consistently repressed across these neighbors (consensus -0.622), consistent with an anti-angiogenic action.

step6_report.bridge_text: Chemistry places Trametinib nearest Palbociclib (CDK inhibitor); its interpolated phenotype places it nearest Mercaptopurine (Antimetabolite). The two routes differ.
step6_report.caveat: Illustrative proof-of-concept on the 94-compound MegaFin zebrafish atlas. Chemistry (structure, descriptors, neighbors) is real; phenotype and organ readouts are synthesized per drug-class as placeholders, pending the released MegaFin single-cell dataset.
